title: Bram and the Bell
premise: Marguerite Coldharbour, a pest controller with an unusual specialty in infestations that leave fingerprints, is hired to clear Coldharbour Hall, the ancestral house she never knew bore her name. The sleep recordings she installs to monitor the 'pest' capture a second voice answering questions no one asks aloud, and Marguerite realizes the intruder is not in the house — it is the house, wearing her inherited face. To survive, she must complete the founding ritual the original Coldharbours abandoned halfway: a naming ceremony that binds one living descendant to the walls forever. In the end, Marguerite finishes the ritual but speaks her own name instead of the founder's, unbinding the house and freeing the trapped voices — at the cost of the family name itself.
about_author: Vesper Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing estate sales and unclaimed inheritances. They write horror about houses that remember their owners better than the owners do.

chapters.title: The Fingerprinted Door
chapters.summary: Marguerite arrives at Coldharbour Hall after a terse letter offering triple her usual fee. Every interior door bears small, greasy handprints at shoulder height — fresh each morning despite locked rooms. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: wary professionalism masking a strange pull of familiarity toward the house.

chapters.title: Lights On, Doors Counted
chapters.summary: Marguerite establishes her routines: counting doors (there are thirteen by day, fourteen by night), keeping every light burning, and setting up audio recorders in the bedrooms. She finds her own surname in the founder's portrait plaque and assumes coincidence. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: control as comfort, beginning to crack.

chapters.title: What the Recorder Keeps
chapters.summary: Reviewing the first night's tapes, Marguerite hears herself talking in her sleep — and a second voice, dry as paper, answering questions she never asked aloud. The voice knows her childhood nickname. POV: Marguerite, with transcript interludes. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Thirteen or Fourteen
chapters.summary: Marguerite maps the house and confirms the extra door appears only after midnight, always on a different wall. Behind it once, briefly: a corridor lined with coats, all bearing her name tag. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: vertigo — the house is rearranging itself around her.

chapters.title: The Local Historian
chapters.summary: In town, Marguerite meets Odile Vasseur, an elderly archivist who recognizes her face instantly: 'You have the founder's chin.' Odile reveals the Coldharbours died out in 1974 — or were absorbed. POV: Marguerite, then a brief Odile section. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as something less like legacy, more like predation.

chapters.title: Questions Answered
chapters.summary: Marguerite deliberately asks a question aloud before sleeping. The recording captures the second voice replying in detail — about the ritual, about 'the finishing,' about how the founders stopped halfway and left the house hungry. POV: Marguerite with transcripts. Emotional beat: terror braided with terrible temptation; the voice offers belonging.

chapters.title: Halfway House
chapters.summary: Odile shares the founders' journal: a binding rite meant to anchor the family into the hall's foundations, interrupted when the last Coldharbour fled mid-ceremony. Since then, the house has been trying to finish it alone, wearing borrowed faces. POV: Odile's 1974 flashback interwoven with Marguerite's present. Emotional beat: grief for the fled ancestor, recognition of the pattern repeating.

chapters.title: The Coat Corridor
chapters.summary: Marguerite finds the fourteenth door standing open at dusk and walks the coat corridor. Each coat fits her. At its end, a mirror shows her reflection continuing to move after she stops. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: identity dissolving; she can no longer be sure which movements are hers.

chapters.title: Sleepwalking Sessions
chapters.summary: The recordings now show Marguerite leaving her bed nightly, answering the voice's questions in turn — her own voice growing drier, more papery. She nails her bedroom door shut; it is open by morning anyway. POV: Marguerite reading her own transcripts. Emotional beat: horror at being both investigator and infestation.

chapters.title: Odile's Warning
chapters.summary: Odile begs Marguerite to leave before the winter solstice, when the ritual's 'open door' closes for another generation. Leaving means the house takes someone else; staying means it takes her. Marguerite refuses — the pull of finally belonging somewhere outweighs fear. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: tragic stubbornness; belonging weaponized.

chapters.title: The Founder's Face
chapters.summary: Marguerite wakes to find the founder's portrait repainted overnight — now unmistakably her own likeness, aged forty years. The greasy handprints spell out a word on her door: SOON. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: the horror of being expected, awaited, claimed.

chapters.title: Under the Floors
chapters.summary: Following scratching sounds, Marguerite pries up the cellar floor and finds the founders' half-built ritual circle: thirteen name-stones set, a fourteenth socket empty and warm. The trapped voices whisper from the mortar. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: revulsion mixed with pity — the house is full of people who never got to finish.

chapters.title: The Voice Explains Itself
chapters.summary: In the longest recording yet, the second voice tells its story: it was the first Coldharbour, bound incomplete, conscious in the walls for two centuries, wearing descendants' faces just to be asked a question again. POV: the entity's monologue over Marguerite's listening silence. Emotional beat: sympathy curdling into understanding — it doesn't want company, it wants completion.

chapters.title: Counting Backwards
chapters.summary: The lights begin failing room by room, and the day-count of doors drops to twelve. Marguerite realizes the house is closing itself around her, sealing exits, rationing darkness. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: claustrophobic urgency; time made physical.

chapters.title: Odile Comes to the Hall
chapters.summary: Odile arrives against her own advice, carrying the founders' missing ritual page recovered from a burned chapel. She admits she has her own reason: her grandmother was the fleeing Coldharbour's companion, and the guilt has passed down like the name did. POV: dual. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; two inheritances of unfinished business.

chapters.title: The Terms of Finishing
chapters.summary: Deciphering the page, they learn the ritual requires a descendant to speak their full name into the empty stone socket while the house holds them — binding them forever. But a loophole glimmers: the rite binds 'the name,' not necessarily the speaker. POV: Marguerite and Odile debating through the night. Emotional beat: desperate hope, moral weight of any choice.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: The final door disappears. The house walks Marguerite sleeping down to the cellar, where the thirteenth stones glow faintly and the empty socket waits, steaming in the cold. Odile follows the sound of Marguerite's sleep-voice reciting the liturgy. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: the trap springing; tenderness inside terror.

chapters.title: The Ceremony Interrupted, Again
chapters.summary: Odile breaks the trance, and the house retaliates — walls breathing inward, the founder's voice speaking through Marguerite's mouth, demanding its name back. They fight to reach the socket before dawn completes the binding without consent. POV: rapid alternation. Emotional beat: climax of will against inheritance.

chapters.title: A Name Spoken
chapters.summary: At the socket, Marguerite understands the loophole: she gives the stone not her name but the house's own founding name, 'Coldharbour' itself, spoken as a renunciation. The binding seizes the name, not the woman. The hall convulses. POV: Marguerite, present-tense intensity. Emotional beat: sacrificial clarity — giving up the family name to keep the self.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Dawn floods the cellar. The voices leave the mortar one by one, thanking her in borrowed tones, until only the first Coldharbour remains — and chooses, at last, to stop rather than be finished. The fourteenth door opens onto ordinary morning air. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: release, exhaustion, unexpected mourning for the monster.

chapters.title: After the Count
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Marguerite returns to find the hall ordinary: thirteen doors, cold hearths, blank portraits. Odile records a final interview in which Marguerite, asked her full name, hesitates — 'Coldharbour' belongs to the stone now, and she must choose what to call herself. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: identity as chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: The Bell
chapters.summary: On leaving, Marguerite finds a small bronze bell on the doorstep, warm as a held hand — the founders' calling bell, returned. When she rings it, nothing answers, and the silence sounds like freedom. She keeps it, not as a warning, but as proof she finished what others couldn't, her own way. POV: Marguerite, closing reflection. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; belonging found in the act of letting go.
